executive_summary.headline: Agents go always-on for everyday users
executive_summary.body: Anthropic's Claude Duet, Notion's rebuilt 24-hour Agents and a WhatsApp assistant called readywhen all shipped this week. The shared idea: the agent watches and acts without a prompt. Duet is a research preview for US Pro and Max subscribers.

executive_summary.headline: Gemini goes after small business owners
executive_summary.body: Google added a business hub, brand-style memory, finance skills and connected apps (Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho, Xero). It rolls out to all Gemini app users over the coming days.

executive_summary.headline: Small open models keep closing the gap
executive_summary.body: Recursive's free Flint runs on a laptop at 125+ tokens per second and claims to lead mixture-of-experts models under 50B parameters on agentic coding benchmarks. Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro brings a 1M-token context, with weights due by Nov 4.

executive_summary.headline: AI for science had a strong week
executive_summary.body: Hugging Face Bio's open Carbon-X reads DNA in chat at about 1/1,800 of GPT-6.1 Sol's per-problem cost. OpenAI reported thousands of agents building a brain-cell reasoning atlas in 32 minutes. Ai2 shipped global satellite embeddings, and zCAD.AI turns prompts into STEP files.

executive_summary.headline: Voice agents get cheaper and broader
executive_summary.body: Mistral's Voxtral 3 lists a full voice agent at $0.04 per minute, and ElevenLabs launched Eleven Realtime with 90+ languages.

top_picks.title: Gemini adds a business hub, brand-kit visuals and finance skills for small business owners
top_picks.summary: Gemini gets a business landing page, brand style you define by uploading a site, kit, fonts or palette (paired with Nano Banana 2.1 for on-brand visuals), and finance skills that turn messy spreadsheets and receipts into charts and interactive models. Connected apps include Adobe, Canva, Dropbox, Shopify, Wix, Zoho and Xero, plus Google Business Profile, Ads and Workspace, rolling out globally to all Gemini app users in the coming days.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: upload your brand kit once and generate every campaign asset on-brand. Feed it last month's receipts and ask for the chart you never had time to build.
top_picks.pricing: Rolling out to all Gemini app users; no paid-plan requirement stated.
top_picks.competitive_context: Canva and Wix are connected apps rather than rivals here, so Gemini becomes the front door to the small-business toolchain.
key_takeaways: Business landing page with marketing and finance skills.
Brand style is retained across sessions.
Rollout is global over the coming days.

top_picks.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro with a 1M-token context
top_picks.summary: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 3T-class open-weight model with a 1-million-token context and gains in coding, 3D creation and financial research. A Highspeed variant runs 2 to 3 times faster; both are live on Kimi.com, the mobile apps, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the API (kimi-k3.1-pro), with full weights promised by Nov 4. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: point it at your longest document pile (a year of reports, a whole repo) and ask for the contradictions. Compare with your current model on one real task.
top_picks.pricing: Not stated on the announcement page.
top_picks.competitive_context: Lands the same week as Recursive's laptop-sized Flint, showing open weights at both ends of the size range.
key_takeaways: 3T-class, 1M context.
Highspeed tier is 2 to 3x faster, per Moonshot.
Weights due by Nov 4.
On a stress test, Moonshot reports claim-level hallucination fell from 23.4% (K3) to 8.3%, and notes this does not represent everyday error rates.

top_picks.title: Recursive releases Flint, a free laptop coding model built largely by its own research system
top_picks.summary: Flint is a 40B mixture-of-experts coding model that activates 2.5B parameters per token, released under Apache 2.0 with a 512k-token context. Recursive reports more than 125 tokens per second on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and more than 150 on a 64GB NVIDIA RTX Spark at short context, and says its Eureka Machine research system contributed to data, training, quantization and inference work.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a private coding agent on your own laptop, offline and fee-free. Give it one small internal tool to build this weekend.
top_picks.competitive_context: Recursive claims it beats other mixture-of-experts models under 50B parameters and rivals 25B to 40B dense models while running over 5x faster.
key_takeaways: Works with llama.cpp, Ollama, Unsloth, LM Studio, vLLM and SGLang.
Recursive ships a lightweight inference engine, rec, tuned for M4 Pro and M5 Pro/Max.
Recursive says it may need smaller subtasks and more explicit instructions than larger closed coding models.
top_picks.results: Company-reported on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench Verified; the announcement page publishes no absolute scores.

top_picks.title: Hugging Face Bio releases Carbon-X, an open model that reads DNA in plain-English chat
top_picks.summary: Carbon-X is a 14.8B open model (Apache 2.0) trained on 302B tokens of mid-training data that handles raw DNA sequence alongside text. It averages 66.7% across five DNA benchmarks with thinking off versus 67.5% for GPT-6.1 Sol, at about 1/1,800 of the inference cost per problem, and its weights fit on one 80 GB GPU.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: show a skeptical scientist their own sequence data answered in plain English on their own GPU. Costing a ClinVar-scale sweep at about $300 is the demo that lands.
top_picks.competitive_context: Hugging Face's own benchmark comparison; independent replication is not yet available.
key_takeaways: Hugging Face estimates analyzing 2.4M ClinVar variants of uncertain significance at about $300 versus $32,000 to $4M on evaluated frontier models.
Serves with vLLM on a single GPU.
Research starting point: not clinically validated and not for medical decisions.
top_picks.results: Company-reported: 66.7% average over five DNA benchmarks versus 67.5% for GPT-6.1 Sol.

top_picks.title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 for voice agents
top_picks.summary: Voxtral 3 bundles speech-to-text in 50+ languages, text-to-speech in 35+ languages with emotional delivery, and deep tool use in one voice-agent SDK that works with LiveKit. Mistral lists $0.0035 per minute for batch transcription, $0.008 realtime, and $0.04 per minute for a full voice agent on Mistral Small 4.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a bakery-style phone-order agent is now a weekend project at a few cents a minute. Prototype your most repetitive inbound call.
top_picks.pricing: STT $0.0035/min batch, $0.008/min realtime; TTS $13 per 1M characters; voice agent $0.04/min.
top_picks.competitive_context: Eleven Realtime from ElevenLabs landed the same week, so voice-agent stacks now have two serious new options.
key_takeaways: 50+ STT languages, 35+ TTS languages.
LiveKit SDK for real-time use.
Published per-minute pricing.

top_picks.title: zCAD.AI turns prompts into real CAD parts with STEP export
top_picks.summary: zCAD.AI generates parametric 3D parts, not just meshes, and exports STEP on every plan. The free tier gives 200 credits a month with public models and training data; it was the top Product Hunt launch on Oct 24.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: have an engineer describe a bracket or fixture in a sentence and see if the STEP file opens cleanly in their CAD tool. Fast jigs and mockups are the first win.
top_picks.pricing: Free: 200 credits a month; STEP export on all plans.
top_picks.competitive_context: Last week's SolidCraft was open-source parametric CAD; zCAD is the hosted, prompt-first counterpart.
key_takeaways: Real editable parts rather than shapes.
STEP export on every plan.
Free plan models are public.

sections.title: Product Hunt
sections.description: Top AI launches of the week by upvotes. Maker site first, Product Hunt page second. Claude Duet and zCAD.AI also launched on Product Hunt and appear in Top Picks.

items.title: Beam.win
items.summary: Run AI agents on one Mac and use their windows on another: terminals, browsers and app windows appear as native windows with Dock icons, encrypted between your Macs. Free to try for 20 minutes a day. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: park long-running agent jobs on a spare Mac mini and work from the laptop in front of you.

items.title: DeepCell
items.summary: Builds ready-to-use spreadsheets, documents and slides for deadline work such as budget forecasts and monthly reports, with sources and edits that propagate through related parts. Uses a new .deepcell format; free per the listing. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand it next month's forecast deck and see whether one edit really updates the whole model.

items.title: Composio Instant
items.summary: Tagline: the easiest way for AI agents to pay for their own tools. An SDK aimed at developers wiring agents to paid APIs. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give a side-project agent a small budget and let it buy the tools it needs.

items.title: UseIt Studio
items.summary: An AI design studio for physical items: describe a pin, sticker, gift box or pop-up card and get an editable file with real dimensions, bleed and dielines, ready to print, cut and fold. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: design your own event swag or packaging mockups in one sentence and send the file to a print shop.

items.title: BAND for Developers
items.summary: Tagline: coordinate and govern multi-agent work in a single chat. A shared interaction layer with built-in governance for agents and people; the launch was titled BAND for Developers (coding agents, meet teamwork). Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: put a drafting agent and a reviewing agent in one shared thread and watch how they hand off.

items.title: MOVO AI
items.summary: A long-form video agent for mobile: shoot, upload or start with an idea, and it plans, creates, keeps characters and scenes consistent, and keeps working while the phone is locked. Free options listed. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: turn a phone clip and a one-line brief into a finished explainer while you do something else.

items.title: Needle
items.summary: An agent-native outbound engine: prompt Claude, ChatGPT or Grok to find, enrich and contact leads on LinkedIn, Instagram or email. Launch offer: code PH2026 for 50% off six months after a 7-day trial. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a whole outreach list from one prompt and compare reply rates with your manual list.

items.title: Doneas
items.summary: A daily 15-minute accountability call with five other builders, a Monday planning ritual and a public progress page for solo founders. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: copy the format for an internal builders' circle, with a Monday plan and a public ship log.

items.title: myPip
items.summary: Describe a game and it builds a playable browser version you can publish and monetize, with multiplayer, in-app purchases and ads. Free per the listing. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: prototype a training game or a quiz in an afternoon and share a link.

items.title: readywhen
items.summary: A personal assistant that lives inside WhatsApp and handles errands and scheduling the way a senior assistant would. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: try delegating one week of scheduling to a chat-based assistant and count the hours back.

items.title: TwinMind for Desktop
items.summary: TwinMind now runs natively on Mac and Windows: it auto-detects meetings in Zoom, Meet and other apps, gives live transcripts and summaries in 140+ languages, and adds a hotkey dictation mic that pastes cleaned-up text into any app. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let a memory assistant listen to a week of meetings and ask it what you promised.

items.title: AgentValley
items.summary: An open-source Mac notch app that shows every running Claude Code agent at a glance. Votes are Product Hunt daily-leaderboard counts at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: a tiny status display for parallel agents is a good first weekend build.

sections.title: Frontier and Specialist Models
sections.description: New model and API releases from Oct 19 to 25. Kimi K3.1 Pro, Flint, Carbon-X and Voxtral 3 are in Top Picks.

items.title: OpenAI makes the Decisions API generally available
items.summary: The Decisions API on gpt-6-luna is GA: up to 10x faster than the Responses API, 400 questions per request, input at $0.10 per million tokens ($0.01 cached) and no output charge. OpenAI lists Box, Datadog, Ramp, Sierra and Speak as customers.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: batch hundreds of yes/no or classification calls through one request. Re-run your messiest tagging job and compare cost and time.
items.pricing: $0.10 per 1M input tokens, $0.01 cached input, no output charge.
items.competitive_context: Also this week: 12-hour prompt caching, with cache writes billed at 2.5x the input price.

items.title: ElevenLabs launches Eleven Realtime, Mini and Max
items.summary: Eleven Realtime v1 ships in Mini and Max sizes with 90+ languages, 17,000+ voices and an OpenAI Realtime-compatible API. ElevenLabs cites 98.8% on Big Bench Audio for Max, per Artificial Analysis.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: swap it into an existing realtime voice prototype through the compatible API and A/B the voices.
items.pricing: Not stated in the launch post.

items.title: Cloudflare previews Clairic, an extraction model on Workers AI
items.summary: Clairic is a data-extraction model that returns structured fields without generating output tokens, in under a second, in preview on Workers AI. Cloudflare plans open weights and reports 3.3% average error on a TSA wait-time forecast.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: point it at invoices or forms and get clean fields back in under a second. Replace one fragile regex pipeline.
items.pricing: Preview on Workers AI; pricing not stated.

items.title: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps use thousands of agents to build a brain-cell reasoning atlas
items.summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research had thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents work through a whole-brain CRISPR atlas in 32 minutes. At the largest workload the distributed agents cited more than 700 references versus 11 for one agent, and blinded experts preferred the distributed reports 75% of the time. The proposed mechanisms are leads that still need experiments.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: split one literature-heavy research question across many parallel agents and compare against a single-agent run. Count the citations each one finds.
items.pricing: Not stated; research results rather than a product release.
items.competitive_context: Pairs with the Orchestra Bio acquisition announced the day before.
key_takeaways: Many agents in parallel beat one agent on breadth of evidence at fixed model and resources.
Expert preference of 75% is OpenAI's reported figure.
OpenAI describes the outputs as promising leads, not confirmed findings.
items.results: OpenAI-reported: more than 700 references versus 11; experts preferred the output 75% of the time.

sections.title: YC and Startups
sections.description: No YC launch could be tied to a date in this window from the public page, so this section carries startups only.

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Orchestra Bio
items.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Orchestra Bio, a platform where biopharma teams and AI agents coordinate drug-development programs, and will combine it with Rosalind. OpenAI names Novo Nordisk and Moderna as partners; no deal terms are stated.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: watch how a frontier lab folds a domain startup in, then ask which of your own research workflows could use the same pairing.
items.competitive_context: Announced the day before the brain-cell atlas results.

items.title: Tend: personal AI for businesses and entrepreneurs
items.summary: Tend is an early personal AI assistant aimed at small-business owners and entrepreneurs; it drew 86 points on its Product Hunt launch week.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: sample how a solo founder frames a personal AI for business before you scope one.

sections.title: Consumer, Creator and Small Business
sections.description: Everyday AI features and creator tools worth trying this month.

items.title: Gemini Personal Intelligence now reads your Maps searches and saved places
items.summary: With permission, Gemini can reference Google Maps searches and saved places alongside Calendar to suggest where to eat after your last meeting. 9to5Google also reports AI Ultra subscribers are being told Gemini 4 Argon will replace Deep Think soon.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask for a dinner spot near your last meeting and see whether saved places beat a search.
items.competitive_context: Google's announcement was a Gemini app post on X dated Oct 22; its direct URL was not retrievable, so 9to5Google is the linked reporting.

items.title: Notion rebuilds Agents to run for hours and adds Auto
items.summary: Notion rebuilt its agent harness: Agents now get their own computer and browser and can work for up to 24 hours. Auto, the upgraded model router, delivered results similar to Opus 5.5 and Astra at about 90% lower average cost across 20+ common tasks, per Notion. A personal Agent can connect a ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Go plan, and a new credit system unifies AI usage.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand an agent your messiest weekly report, use Review for me, and let it run overnight.

items.title: Canva Craft image model arrives with editable, design-ready output
items.summary: Canva's public documentation lists Craft-1 2K, an image generation model trained on more than 1 billion images plus structured JSON layouts, with an EU market placement date of Oct 22. The Product Hunt listing pitches design-ready images you can edit. A standalone Canva launch post was not located.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: generate a campaign image, then edit it layer by layer in the same tool.
items.competitive_context: Canva's documentation is the primary source; a dedicated launch post was not located.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive agent app
items.summary: Claude Duet is a proactive agent app that watches for what needs your attention and acts on it. It ships as a research preview behind a waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on iOS, Android and claude.ai, built around Opus 5.5 with more than 6,000 Marketplace connectors.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let an agent triage your day instead of waiting for prompts. Connect email and calendar, then see what it surfaces by Friday that you would have missed.
items.pricing: Included in Pro and Max usage limits; waitlist, US only at launch.
items.competitive_context: Joins Notion's rebuilt background agents and readywhen's WhatsApp assistant in a week where agents moved from chat boxes to always-on helpers.
key_takeaways: Research preview, waitlist, US Pro and Max.
Opus 5.5 under the hood.
6,000+ Marketplace connectors at launch.
Early users include a restaurant owner and a real-estate broker, per Anthropic.
items.why_it_matters: The proactive-agent pattern is now a shipped consumer product from a frontier lab.

items.title: Google Cloud introduces Agent Compute Engine
items.summary: Agent Compute Engine runs agents in microVMs, with open-source Agent Substrate supporting 200,000 agents, 500 activations per second and sub-500 ms resume, per Google.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: borrow the pause-and-resume pattern so idle agents cost nothing between tasks.

sections.title: Funding
sections.description: Rounds verified against the company's own announcement. Rounds found only in press roundups are listed under flagged items.

items.title: Daytona raises $60M Series B at a $1B valuation for agent sandboxes
items.summary: Daytona raised $60 million led by FirstMark Growth at a $1 billion valuation, bringing total funding to $91 million, with Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next and Okta Ventures as strategics. The company reports roughly 25x revenue growth since January and about 135% average monthly net revenue retention.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: the sandbox layer is where agent builders spend; try one on your next agent project.
items.results: Company-reported: about 25x revenue growth since January; Writer provisioned 300,000 sandboxes in a month.

items.title: Otter.ai closes $320M growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund
items.summary: Otter.ai announced the closing of $320 million in growth financing from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund on Oct 20. The company says the capital will fund enterprise growth, go-to-market, international expansion and enterprise agentic workflows.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: the meeting transcript is becoming a company knowledge base; try querying a month of your own notes.

sections.title: Open Source
sections.description: Open weights and open data releases. Flint and Carbon-X are in Top Picks.

items.title: Ai2 releases OlmoEarth v1.3 with global 10 m satellite embeddings
items.summary: OlmoEarth v1.3 adds precomputed embeddings for every 10-meter square of the world's land across multiple years, plus a browser Embeddings Explorer that needs no sign-in. Models, data and code can be downloaded with no invitation.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pick one site, find similar land cover across the planet and compare two years for change. Useful for siting, climate and materials-exposure questions.

items.title: Mistral and NVIDIA team up on AI-native engineering and physics benchmarks
items.summary: Mistral and NVIDIA will build closed-loop engineering workflows and public benchmarks plus open datasets for physics models and for agents doing CAE and EDA work. Mistral says Large 4 weights are planned for the end of October.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use the coming open physics benchmarks to test how well any model handles a simulation problem from your own field.

emerging_signals.pattern: Proactive, background agents reach mainstream apps
emerging_signals.evidence: Claude Duet, Notion's 24-hour Agents and Auto, readywhen on WhatsApp and MOVO AI's lock-screen video agent all launched within five days.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether usage-based credits or flat plans win, and how fast Duet leaves waitlist.

emerging_signals.pattern: Biology models are shrinking and going open
emerging_signals.evidence: Carbon-X (14.8B, Apache 2.0, one 80 GB GPU) approaches a frontier model's DNA benchmark average, per Hugging Face.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Independent replication on private sequence sets.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agent infrastructure is attracting growth capital
emerging_signals.evidence: Daytona's $60M Series B at $1B and Google's Agent Compute Engine landed in the same week.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether sandbox pricing converges on per-second billing.

suggested_refinements.notes: Source gaps this week: Product Hunt returns 403 to automated page checks, so product pages were read through the fetch tool and maker sites were checked for HTTP 200 with curl. The Launch YC page shows only relative dates, so no YC launch was dated into the window. Mistral, Anthropic, x.ai and TechCrunch index pages list titles without links, so individual URLs were resolved by search. Several funding roundups lacked company announcements; only Daytona and Otter.ai were confirmed against company posts. Product Hunt counts for Oct 25 are partial. Carbon-X date comes from the Hugging Face model page metadata (Oct 22); Kimi K3.1 Pro date comes from the Kimi blog index (Oct 24) because the post itself is undated; OlmoEarth v1.3 date comes from the Ai2 research page listing (Oct 22). Notion, Canva and Gemini Personal Intelligence entries rely on release notes, model documentation and a 9to5Google report because a standalone launch post was not retrieved.
